subject: Re: Contract term, staged auto-renew and termination-for-convenience implementation playbook
messages:
From: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@brightlinehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T14:05:00Z
Subject: Initial redlines: auto-renew notice and TFC parameters

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement ran a quick review of the MSA + Order Form and attached a short redline summary focusing on term and offboarding: Brightline_Term_Redlines.pdf (3 pages). The main asks are: 

- Shorten the auto-renew notice from 60 days to 30 days for pilot and small accounts; keep 60 days for enterprise T&Cs.
- Add an explicit 30-day cure period for non-payment before suspension.
- Termination for convenience: Brightline requests a 60-day handover period instead of Redwood's 90 days and a cap on termination fees equal to 25% of remaining committed MRR.

We want to surface any operational impact before we escalate to legal. Can your team confirm whether staged notice (different notice windows by commitment tier) is workable operationally and whether Redwood has an existing playbook for a 30->60 day split? If helpful, I can share our internal runbook.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync on Thursday (8/31) or Friday (9/1) morning PST? Please propose a time and any pre-read.

Best,
Thomas
Director, Procurement
Brightline Health

Attachments: Brightline_Term_Redlines.pdf (summary of redline requests)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: auto-renew notice and TFC parameters

Thomas —

Thanks for the note and for the redline PDF. High level: staged notice windows are something we've implemented before (pilot-class accounts vs enterprise commitments) but it requires a short addendum on the Order Form and an operational tag on the customer record so billing and renewal reminders align. I attached our internal playbook (redwood_term_playbook_v1.docx) which outlines the options and run-of-play for offboarding. 

Quick answers to your asks: 

- Notice windows: We can support 30-day for pilots (<$50k ARR) and 60-day for enterprise by adding an Order Form field (RenewalNoticeTier = Pilot|Enterprise). That will change reminder cadence and the escalation path. 
- Cure period: 30-day cure for non-payment is standard; we can preserve suspension after 30 days but prefer 10-day billing reminder + 20-day final notice before service action. We can show the exact timeline in the addendum.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): 60 days is workable for Brightline; the termination fee cap is a commercial ask. Standard Redwood posture is transition support with a 90-day default to protect stateful migrations, but we can offer 60 days + a capped transition fee for enterprise-level commitments to compensate for data egress and runbook effort. For pilots, we can waive the fee.

Proposed next steps: 
1) 30-minute call to align commercial vs legal redlines (I can include Ben from Sales and Marissa from Legal).
2) Post-call we will produce a short Order Form addendum draft that sets RenewalNoticeTier, Cure timeline, and TFC mechanics.
3) If you want, we'll provide a mock timeline and billing events extract so your procurement team can validate the cadence.

I'm available 9/1 09:00-11:00 PST or 8/31 14:00-16:00 PST. Book a slot on the pre-call deck link below if either works.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_term_playbook_v1.docx
Related link: https://redwood.app/decks/BR-7834/precall

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: auto-renew notice and TFC parameters

Diego / Ben —

Looping in quick legal guidance inline before we take this to Brightline legal: 

- Order Form Addendum: Simple table; one line item for RenewalNoticeTier with values and a default of 60 days. Example language: "For Pilot Accounts (as defined in Addendum A), the renewal notice period shall be 30 days; for Enterprise Accounts the renewal notice period shall be 60 days."

- Cure/suspension: We prefer preserving a 30-day cure overall but split the notices as Diego suggested (10/20 cadence). That will keep collections playbook intact.

- TFC: We should avoid an uncapped percentage tied to remaining MRR. Counterproposal: 60-day handover + either (a) a fixed transition fee equal to one month's average committed MRR or (b) a tiered cap (25% for commitments > $500k ARR, waived for pilots). Both give commercial predictability.

I'm drafting specific redline snippets; Diego/Ben, if you approve, I'll attach them to the pre-call deck and include in the addendum draft for Brightline. Keep the call to 30 minutes and have procurement + legal on their side.

—Marissa
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Contract term, staged auto-renew and termination-for-convenience implementation playbook

Diego / Marissa / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clarity. 9/1 09:00 PST was a bit tight on our end, but 09:30 PST works for our procurement lead and counsel. We accept the suggested framework: staged RenewalNoticeTier (pilot/enterprise), 30-day cure with the 10/20 reminder split, and 60-day TFC handover for Brightline with a proposed cap — we prefer the tiered cap approach you mentioned in your reply. 

I've uploaded a short pre-call summary (precall_summary_slide.pdf) and added a placeholder DocuSign link for the NDA cover sheet we use for addenda: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BR-7834. Please include any suggested redline snippets in the pre-read so we can come prepared.

I'll join the 09:30 PST call via the calendar invite. See you then.

Thanks,
Thomas Reed
Director, Procurement
Brightline Health
